title: Value data source: an operator filter with a plain-object comparand ($ne, $notContains, ordering, $nin) still serves rows instead of being refused
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CajiB6BSQKWowy6YLB

From the narrowing contract review of PR #35423 (seat 5, at `a5945f2a`; ungraded finding, for a card). Parent: #34990.

## Defect
PR #35423 makes `ValueDataSource` (the in-memory `provider: 'value'` source, `ui/packages/core/src/adapters/ValueDataSource.ts`) refuse a plain-object comparand with no `$` key on the AST arm (`['f', '!=', { owner: 'u1' }]` and the other comparand-reading operators). The object-dialect twin still answers: an operator map such as `{ f: { $ne: { owner: 'u1' } } }`, `$notContains`, the ordering operators (`$gt` / `$gte` / `$lt` / `$lte`) and `$nin` with such an object compare it by reference or as the text `[object Object]`. So `$ne` and `$notContains` serve every row, and ordering serves some rows. The spec's comparand door (`normalizeFieldSpec` → `judgeLiteralComparand`) refuses the same comparand, so this is the value source failing open where the platform refuses.

## Done when
`matchesDollarOperator` gives a plain-object, no-`$` comparand under those operators the same named refusal as the AST arm (one builder, as `nestedRelationRefusalReason`), with pins per operator and a CONTROL (a scalar comparand, a `Date`, a `{ $field }` reference still answer). It is a narrowing of a published export: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with BREAKING, an ADR-0087 marker, and the dogfood battery.

## Grade
p2 · area:data · domain:ui. Wrong rows (every row on `$ne` / `$notContains`) on value-provider views, no refusal; the same class as #35447.
